title: Semicompleteness of the hypercube division sequences
statement: Let $C_M^N$ denote the maximum number of pieces into which an $M$-dimensional hypercube can be cut using $N-1$ hyperplanes, and let $\{C_M^N\}$ be the resulting sequence as $N$ varies. A sequence of positive, strictly increasing integers is **semicomplete** if, for every $j>2$ and every natural number $k<\lfloor G\rfloor$, the integer $k$ can be represented as a sum of distinct terms from the first $j$ sequence terms divided by $j$, where $G$ is the sum of those $j$ fractions. **The hypercube division conjecture.** The sequence $\{C_M^N\}$ is semicomplete for every natural number $M\geq 1$. This would establish semicompleteness for an infinite family of sequences; the cases $M=1,2,3,4$ are proved in the paper, while the general case remains open.
